chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Uyayna, from Umar ibn Yazeed who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The gratitude for every blessing, even if it is great, is that you praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of true gratitude for a blessing in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distills the comprehensive concept of shukr into its fundamental act of verbal praise (hamd), asserting that the magnitude of the blessing is secondary to the sincerity of the acknowledgment. This aligns with Shia theological emphasis on gratitude as a continuous state of consciousness rather than a reaction solely to major events, reinforcing the idea that every blessing, no matter how small, warrants explicit recognition of Allah’s generosity. The hadith serves as a practical guideline for believers to cultivate a habit of constant thankfulness, ensuring that spiritual growth is not hindered by overlooking minor favors.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Uyayna, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> saying: ‘Gratefulness for each Bounty, and even if it is great is that you Praise Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn ‘Uyayna from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Expressing one’s thankfulness for any favor, no matter how great it may be, is to thank Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, for it.’”
